findings.place: Opening word, line 1
findings.evidence: Crop 01 shows a capital with a roof and baseline, followed by a second tall descending stroke and a detached short crossbar to its right. The last low strokes are too reduced to separate em from ou securely. The second tall/crossed form supports Item as the first reading; the alternatives remain open. H’s Ici does not account for that tall crossed form.
findings.mathematical_note: No mathematical cue determined this word.

findings.place: Short form before application, line 3
findings.evidence: Crop 02 shows two tall strokes sharing a crossing, then a short terminal curve at the baseline. There are no separate intervening o/u bodies. The written contracted group is tte; C’s primary reading is resolved rather than changed.

findings.place: Relation between X and S-star, line 4
findings.evidence: Crop 03 shows a long near-horizontal shaft, a thickened right endpoint and a tiny downward stub. A complete two-sided arrowhead is not visible. The shaft-first transcription and arrow alternative are both retained.
findings.mathematical_note: The nearby words application surjective make an arrow a reading cue, but do not supply the missing upper head stroke.

findings.place: Two groups before images, line 4
findings.evidence: Crop 04 shows two separate ink groups before images. The first begins with a tall closed loop and has a low tail. The second has a short upright over a smaller loop, a long low continuation and a downturned end. This favors les des, with les les retained for the compressed second group. The two-group presence is clear even though its second word remains uncertain.
findings.mathematical_note: The grammatical expectation of a single article was not used to remove either group.

findings.place: Overwritten capital at Or, line 6
findings.evidence: Crop 05 shows extra underlying strokes in the O: a left upright, an internal oblique/return and a low curved outline survive beneath the darker live form. They support a possible older D, but the layers cannot be separated securely enough to make its identity and cancelled state certain. Uncertainty therefore surrounds the older deleted-D representation as a whole. The r is live and clear.
findings.mathematical_note: No expansion to a possible earlier word has been supplied.

findings.place: After application, line 7
findings.evidence: Crop 06 separates the faint terminal horizontal of application from a detached dark oblique mark to its lower right, before revient. The detached mark is a comma. C’s comma is resolved; H omits it.

findings.place: Superscript after S in the family index, line 8
findings.evidence: Crop 07 shows a very small high angular mark after the index S: a bent rising stroke and a short right branch are visible. The mark is too reduced to settle asterisk against plus. Both are retained, with the asterisk first. This is a retained C doubt, with no change to H’s primary symbol.
findings.mathematical_note: The same page writes S-star clearly in the earlier equality and application. That repetition supports the first candidate but does not resolve this small mark.

findings.place: Between i.e. and celle, line 8
findings.kind: deletion state (struck given live or live given struck)
findings.evidence: Crop 08 shows the low body of à, a detached grave accent above it, and a heavy separate cancellation across the body. The accent and surviving loop allow à to be read. H gives the cancelled word as live.

findings.place: Before deux familles, line 9
findings.evidence: Crop 09 shows a looped d, a low e and a reinforced terminal s with a downward return beyond the e. The final return supports des. There is no separate cancellation extending across the word. C’s primary des is resolved, and H agrees on the word.
findings.mathematical_note: Agreement with celle and deux familles was secondary to the visible terminal stroke.

findings.place: First sss, before on a les conditions, line 14
findings.evidence: Half b shows three linked low s-like turns; the third has a curved descending/returning stroke, and no independent i-dot is present. The same form is visible again below. The half settled this C doubt, so no crop was made.
findings.mathematical_note: The surrounding conditions explain the abbreviation’s likely expansion, but do not license substituting ssi.

findings.place: Inner parenthetical label after fort que, line 17
findings.evidence: Crop 10 shows two connected centers inside the inner parentheses: the first has a low loop with an ascending diagonal, and the second a separate darker crossed knot to its right. The farther right large curved stroke closes the outer parenthesis. Two stars are legible, resolving C’s primary reading. H has the same primary label.
findings.mathematical_note: Earlier labels on this page provide a comparison for the handwriting; the two visible centers, rather than a presumed logical reference, settle this reading.

findings.place: Correction after d’ordre 2, lines 18–19
findings.kind: deletion state (struck given live or live given struck)
findings.evidence: Crop 11 shows a lower t with a crossbar, a compressed e and a final tall loop/return, all crossed by an independent heavy stroke. The cancelled word is tel. Above it a separate uncancelled et is inserted. H’s single struck et loses both the identity of the lower word and the live state of the raised word. No comma follows this correction in the ink.

findings.place: Connector in final display
findings.evidence: Crop 12 shows a shallow continuous undulation between the two inequalities, with a small initial hook and a downturned right end. Separate o and u bodies are not secure. The reduced ou reading remains first, with a dash alternative. The uncertainty is retained; H’s primary ou has not been changed.
findings.mathematical_note: The adjoining inequalities make a disjunction a reading cue. That cue does not establish the faint letter shapes.

findings.place: Written abbreviation in the raised addition above the family
findings.evidence: Crop 07 shows the compact d’ens group, ending after the low ens strokes, followed by a clear gap before the relation sign. The longer ending embles is not written. Its expansion is recorded only in the abbreviation list.

findings.place: Words H places between d’ens and the nonempty sign
findings.evidence: Crop 07 shows only d’ens, the not-equals sign and the slashed empty-set glyph in the interline. No word groups correspond to deux à deux disjoints. H’s explanatory note also attributes deux à deux to this addition, but the observed addition does not contain those words. The nonempty relation itself is present and is handled separately in F016.
findings.mathematical_note: No disjointness statement has been supplied from the interpretation of an indexed family.

findings.place: Scope and attachment of the raised nonempty relation
findings.evidence: Crop 07 shows the complete raised group d’ens ≠ ∅ above the family and a long curved leader descending to the gap immediately after its index, before the comma. The not-equals sign has two horizontal bars crossed by a short upright/slant; the following glyph has a small oval crossed by a long rising slash. H’s addition macro covers only its expanded d’ensembles, leaving the visible relation outside the insertion.
findings.mathematical_note: The whole visibly linked group is transcribed as an insertion; no extra words are introduced.

findings.place: Punctuation after d’ens in d’ens non vides, line 10
findings.evidence: Half a shows d’ens ending at about x461, then a blank gap before non. No abbreviation full stop appears in that gap. The sentence-final point after vides is present and retained. H adds a point after d’ens.

findings.place: Phrase following à examiner, line 13
findings.evidence: Half b shows the reduced initial avec, a tall descending p in plus, then de and soin, ending with a visible comma. The ink has the sequence avec plus de soin; it has no separate un peu group and the last word has the s/o/i/n pattern rather than près. The phrase was settled from the half.

findings.place: After il donne, line 13
findings.evidence: Half b shows a reduced first n/e group, an accent over the next upper stroke, the low an/moin sequence and the terminal s return. The complete word reads néanmoins, as C gives it. It is sufficiently legible in the half to avoid another crop.

findings.place: Beginning of line 14, before the first sss
findings.evidence: Half b shows ce as a short low group, then qu’on with the long q descender and a detached apostrophe, followed by veut with a small final crossed/upturned t. These three written groups give ce qu’on veut. H leaves part as ill and supplies en général encore in this span; those words do not match its visible groups.

findings.place: Second sss, line 16
findings.evidence: Half b shows the second occurrence as the same series of three linked s-like turns, again with a return on its last stroke and no separate i-dot. It is left in the author’s written form. Its original bounds are given independently of the first occurrence.

findings.place: Adjective after non-parallélisme, line 16
findings.evidence: Half b shows the tall/crossed strokes of strict followed by a separate low final e-like continuation ending to the right. That last letter is preserved in stricte. The adjective is not adjusted to the grammatical gender of non-parallélisme.

findings.place: Underlined word after on a, line 16
findings.evidence: Half b shows two low c/e/c turns and a small final i mark above a single independent underline. The word is ceci. H’s emphasis macro and the supplied underline macro are treated as a convention difference; the lexical reading aussi is the finding.

findings.evidence: Half b shows the underlined ceci followed directly by the opening parenthesis and plus. There is no star label between them. The actual triple-star label appears separately at the start of the bottom condition and is transcribed there.

workflow_feedback: Read only the assigned brief, the supplied pre-scan notation table, scan030 packet, C/H witnesses, C context, C doubt index, supplied preamble and H style, and the three assigned images. No other page, reader output or main-reader decision was inspected.

The whole image was viewed once for layout, each provided half once for a complete ink reading, then one crop was made and viewed once for each genuinely open locus or coherent correction passage. D010 was settled from half b and was not cropped.

All twelve source boxes were checked against the original 1693 by 2365 image bounds before cropping. Processing used Pillow autocontrast, LANCZOS enlargement to 3000 pixels wide and sharpness factor 1.5; no rotation was needed. No accidental source-edge clipping occurred.

Crops include neighboring strokes for context. Crop 07 contains the family index and its interacting raised addition/leader; crop 12 contains the lower correction and final connector. Clear words incidentally visible within those context areas were not cropped again.

The clear H differences received original whole-image bounds even when no crop was made. Several such bounds were tightened through non-OCR dark-pixel extent measurement within manually identified source regions; this did not involve a further visual opening or text recognition.

H’s explicit note about interlinear deux à deux was checked against its actual ink, and no such words were seen. The H style supplies emphasis/uncertainty/addition/deletion conventions but gives no page-specific exact notation mapping requiring another change here. Macro syntax alone has not been counted as a departure.

The complete reading.tex was saved immediately after finishing the image reading and before composing this return. No compilation, OCR, PDF text extraction, external research or mathematical repair was used.
All written code/artifacts from this assignment are confined to work/readers/scan030/R1. The supplied isolated-page workflow and parent delivery instruction determine this intermediate destination.
